**Visual Analysis of Test Image:**
- Field view showing rows of soybean plants with severe yellowing, browning, and wilting
- Dead/dying leaves remaining attached to stems (characteristic)
- Clear contrast between severely affected rows and healthy green plants nearby
- Interveinal chlorosis visible on partially affected leaves
- Whole-plant death pattern progressing through rows

**Comparison with SDS Reference:**
The reference collage for Sudden Death Syndrome shows an almost identical field-level pattern: rows of wilting, yellowed/browned plants with leaves still attached, interspersed with healthy green areas. The close-up leaf shows classic interveinal chlorosis/necrosis. The test image matches this field pattern precisely — widespread plant death in rows while adjacent plants remain green, with leaves staying attached after death.

This strongly aligns with SDS over Phytophthora (which shows chocolate-brown lower stem lesion, not this broad field pattern) or Brown Stem Rot (which shows brown pith specifically).
